title: A shared before/after CompareWidget for Flow results - declared, not per-flow code
description: Every Flow that IMPROVES media the user supplied needs a before/after compare, and it must be ONE piece of code shared by all of them - Fabio, 2026-08-20: "These will happen for other flows as well, so keep that in mind so that we don't have to repeat code. Any flow where there is an improvement to a video ... we will need a CompareWidget. The same thing for any flow for an image that has an improvement or change to an image." First consumer is `ltx-upscale` (MPI-584): source on the LEFT, upscaled on the RIGHT, the draggable reveal bar between them - the same thing the History workspace gives you when two video entries are selected. DO NOT BUILD A COMPARE ENGINE. It exists twice over and both halves are shipped: - `ComparisonManager` + MpiCanvas `activeMode: 'compare'` (js/components/Primitives/MpiCanvas/MpiCanvas.js) owns the reveal bar, `imgAfter`, `sliderPos`, `loadComparisonImage(url)`, `loadComparisonVideo(url,{fps})`, the dual-video RAF sync and the loop flag. It already supports image+image, image+video, video+image and video+video. - `MpiCompareOverlay` (js/components/Compounds/MpiCompareOverlay/) is the HISTORY surface: a full #tool-container takeover on MpiOverlay, opened with `open(itemA,itemB)`, labels, and the hotkey transport (space play/pause both, arrowleft/right frame step, l loop). SO THE JOB IS THE THIRD SURFACE, NOT A THIRD ENGINE. The Flow result pane cannot reuse MpiCompareOverlay as-is: it is a full-screen MpiOverlay takeover with the Stash Pattern, and a Flow is ALREADY an overlay - stacking one inside the other fights the z-order floor and the stash. What is genuinely shared is (a) the canvas compare mode, which is already a Primitive, and (b) the video transport + hotkey block, which today lives INSIDE MpiCompareOverlay and would be the duplicated code Fabio is warning about. PROPOSAL to confirm at pickup: lift that transport/hotkey block into a small shared piece (a Compound `MpiCompareView`, or a util both surfaces call) and make MpiCompareOverlay consume it too, so the History surface and the Flow surface can never drift. Sweep BOTH consumers in one pass - a one-consumer change on a shared primitive is a false done. THE FLOW SIDE STAYS DATA (MPI-572 law: a FlowDef is data a third-party manifest could carry, and MPI-582: every UI element is a component). So the flow DECLARES the compare rather than shipping a component: which media role is the BEFORE. Shape to confirm, e.g. `result: { compare: 'inputVideo' }` on the FlowDef - `inputVideo` for ltx-upscale, `image1` for a future image-improvement flow, ABSENT for a flow with nothing to compare (ltx-foley returns the same pixels; ltx-extend's output is LONGER than its source, so decide deliberately whether a reveal bar means anything there - probably not).
